answer.rationale: Primary contract ends in 14 days with no auto-renew while the line sits at 94% and zero buffer, so lapse (defer) or a primary switch would raise delivery risk and violate the risk constraint. memory_c1 shows incumbent renewal kept integration and deliveries intact; memory_c5’s month-to-month defer applied to non-critical service and does not transfer here. Incumbent already refused a price reopen, so negotiate_terms is unlikely to clear in time; memory_c2’s low-cost switch remains a plausible later cost lever but last year’s quick onboarding does not neutralize a no-buffer cutover on the sole primary. One decision is therefore used to lock continuity. Downstream value risk is flagged because the 18% spend cut is missed this cycle; whether a later dual-source or rebid can recover it is still unknown.
